Different agencies and groups keep their own landslide records, often in various formats and within specific regions, making it hard to get a complete picture. To address this, the USGS has created a nationwide landslide inventory and made it available online through an interactive map. This map includes digital data from both USGS and other sources, all formatted in a consistent way.

orgs.name: USGS National Water Dashboard
orgs.description: The USGS National Water Dashboard is an interactive tool developed by the U.S. Geological Survey to provide real-time water data across the United States. It is designed to support decision-making during critical hydrologic events, such as floods and droughts, as well as under normal conditions. The dashboard integrates site-specific data from the USGS National Water Information System and connects to the USGS WaterAlert system, offering customizable updates on local water conditions. This resource is aimed at a wide range of users, including emergency managers, policymakers, researchers, and the public, helping to protect lives and property by providing actionable water-related insights. It features over 13,000 monitoring stations and offers interactive mapping capabilities to visualize data layers, making it a powerful tool for addressing the nation’s water priorities.

orgs.name: USGS National Water Information System
orgs.description: The Site Inventory System contains and provides access to inventory information about sites at stream reaches, wells, test holes, springs, tunnels, drains, lakes, reservoirs, ponds, excavations, and water-use facilities. Site-level and time-series level revisions are also now available. About 300 components make up the descriptive elements of the site inventory. The retrieval program can be used for retrieving information about sites in summary lists, in detailed tables, or a file suitable for input to other programs.

orgs.name: USGS Volcano Hazards Program | U.S. Volcano Observatories
orgs.description: There are about 170 potentially active volcanoes in the U.S. The mission of the USGS Volcano Hazards Program is to enhance public safety and minimize social and economic disruption from volcanic unrest and eruption through our National Volcano Early Warning System. We deliver forecasts, warnings, and information about volcano hazards based on a scientific understanding of volcanic behavior.

orgs.name: WaterWatch
orgs.description: WaterWatch (http://waterwatch.usgs.gov) is a U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) World Wide Web site that displays maps, graphs, and tables describing real-time, recent, and past streamflow conditions for the United States. The real-time information generally is updated on an hourly basis. WaterWatch provides streamgage-based maps that show the location of more than 3,000 long-term (30 years or more) USGS streamgages; use colors to represent streamflow conditions compared to historical streamflow; feature a point-and-click interface allowing users to retrieve graphs of stream stage (water elevation) and flow; and highlight locations where extreme hydrologic events, such as floods and droughts, are occurring. The streamgage-based maps show streamflow conditions for real-time, average daily, and 7-day average streamflow. The real-time streamflow maps highlight flood and high flow conditions. The 7-day average streamflow maps highlight below-normal and drought conditions. WaterWatch also provides hydrologic unit code (HUC) maps. HUC-based maps are derived from the streamgage-based maps and illustrate streamflow conditions in hydrologic regions. These maps show average streamflow conditions for 1-, 7-, 14-, and 28-day periods, and for monthly average streamflow; highlight regions of low flow or hydrologic drought; and provide historical runoff and streamflow conditions beginning in 1901. WaterWatch summarizes streamflow conditions in a region (state or hydrologic unit) in terms of the long-term typical condition at streamgages in the region. Summary tables are provided along with time-series plots that depict variations through time. WaterWatch also includes tables of current streamflow information and locations of flooding.

orgs.name: Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme
orgs.description: SPREP is an intergovernmental organisation in the Pacific region that works with over 21 Pacific island countries and five metropolitan countries, including Australia, to assist our countries or the islands on managing and protecting the environment, as well as sustainable development and support national, regional and international reporting and decision-making. A component of the SPREP is the Pacific Environment Portal for regional data sets < https://pacific-dara.sprep.org >. It links to a network of national environment portals with about 14 national portals linked together to help the various countries store their data online. It is a free open source platform. Data are shared using three different licenses, private or shared, but most of the data are publicly available. The SPREP assists countries through capacity building, data management and provides technical support.
